# Front CV-axle re-installation techniques

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Clean sealing bits, grease a C-clip, and tap in the front CV-axle while supporting it. [t535]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Clean the sealing bits on both the shaft and differential.
2. Apply a small amount of grease to the C-clip that goes into the differential side.

_Procedure reported by [t535]._

## Tips & gotchas

- [Partial] Use a piece of wood (e.g., 2x8) to support the axle while tapping it in. [t535]
- Support the CV with your thumb and index finger on the LCA saddle if using a hammer. [t535]
- Tap lightly or harder depending on fitment, but avoid forcing too hard. [t535]

## Common mistakes

- Forcing the shaft without centering the C-clip first can damage the diff seal. [t535]
- Using an impact socket to remove the axle nut may shred the threads. [t535]
